title: Isha Koppikar Embraces 'Andh Bhakt' Label in Defiant Pro-India Stand
excerpt: The Bollywood actress responded to online trolling over her political views by declaring herself a 'Bharat Bhakt,' reigniting the diaspora debate over nationalism, dissent, and what it means to love India.
body:
• Bollywood actress Isha Koppikar responded to online trolling by declaring: "Yes, I'm an Andh Bhakt. I'm a Bharat Bhakt," reclaiming the politically charged label as a badge of patriotic pride.
  • Her remarks came after she shared views on democracy and defended Bollywood celebrities criticized for their silence on the CJP protest.
  • Koppikar drew a distinction between criticism of the government and supporting "anti-nationals," sharing a widely circulated note that "opposing BJP is not anti-national, but supporting anti-nationals just to oppose BJP is nothing less than anti-national."
  • The episode reflects a broader cultural fault line that runs through Indian politics and extends deep into the diaspora.

Bollywood actress Isha Koppikar has waded into one of Indian public life's most polarizing debates, embracing the term "Andh Bhakt" — blind devotee — in a pointed response to critics who trolled her over her political views.

"If loving my country makes me a label, so be it. I'd rather be proud than apologetic," Koppikar wrote on Instagram Stories. "Yes, I'm an Andh Bhakt. I'm a Bharat Bhakt."

The declaration came after the actress, known for films like Dil Ka Rishta and Fiza, shared a series of posts defending Bollywood celebrities who faced backlash for their alleged silence over the CJP (Citizens for Justice and Peace) protest. In a separate video, she addressed student protests and urged people to focus on substantive issues rather than online noise.

Reclaiming a Loaded Term

"Andh Bhakt" has become one of Indian political discourse's most weaponized phrases. Originally meaning "blind devotee," it is commonly deployed by critics of the ruling BJP and Prime Minister Narendra Modi to describe supporters they view as uncritical or unquestioning. By claiming it openly, Koppikar joins a growing number of public figures who have attempted to defuse the insult by wearing it as a badge of honor.

"If loving my country makes me a label, so be it. I'd rather be proud than apologetic."

— Isha Koppikar

Her Instagram posts drew predictable reactions from both sides. "Some people will come along now and ask how much money you got from the BJP," one commenter wrote. Another said: "I know mam you're a BJP member, I can understand your stand."

Koppikar also re-shared a widely circulated note that attempted to distinguish between political criticism and anti-national sentiment: "Opposing BJP is not Anti-National. But supporting Anti Nationals Just to oppose BJP is nothing less than anti national."

Democracy, Dictatorship, and the Weight of Words

In a video accompanying her posts, Koppikar addressed the casual use of the term "dictatorship" in Indian political debate. "Democracy does not only mean freedom of speech. Democracy also means freedom of speech and responsibility," she said.

"Dictatorship is where it is not possible to speak against the government or pay a heavy price. Therefore, it is not right to call anything a dictatorship immediately. Words also have a weight," she added, arguing that citizens should both question the government and give credit where it is due.

A Fault Line That Reaches the Diaspora

The debate Koppikar has stepped into extends well beyond Bollywood and India's borders. Within the Indian diaspora, the "bhakt vs. liberal" divide has become a defining feature of community discourse, playing out in living rooms, WhatsApp groups, and community gatherings from New Jersey to the Bay Area.

For NRIs, the question of how to relate to Indian nationalism carries particular complexity. Many maintain deep emotional connections to India while living in democracies with different norms around dissent and political expression. The "Andh Bhakt" label and its reclamation touch on questions of identity, belonging, and the terms on which diaspora Indians engage with their homeland's politics.

Koppikar's stance also reflects a broader shift in how some Indian public figures approach political controversy. Rather than avoiding politically charged topics — long the default strategy in Bollywood — a growing number of celebrities have begun staking out explicit positions, accepting the praise and trolling that follow in equal measure.

"We can all keep our own opinions. We can also ask questions to the government. And when good work is done, it is also necessary to give credit. This is the beauty of democracy."

— Isha Koppikar

Whether framed as patriotism or partisanship, Koppikar's intervention has added another chapter to a debate that shows no signs of resolution — in India or its diaspora.
